RFC9012-13-10.note: TunnelTLV.Preference read through unrecognized short- and long-header sub-TLVs equals the Preference read from the TLV alone; negative shows unrecognized sub-TLVs yield nothing, so they are skipped rather than misread

RFC9012-13-11.note: same unit round-trips the attribute byte-identically and asserts both unrecognized sub-TLVs (1- and 2-octet length headers) are enumerated with values intact

RFC9012-13-12.note: a Preference sub-TLV of the wrong length is skipped (the next well-formed one is used), still enumerated and round-tripped; the negative shows the same type at the right length is used, isolating the malformation as the cause

RFC9012-13-16.note: a VXLAN Encapsulation sub-TLV inside a type-15 TLV does not change the value ze processes (Preference); negative shows a meaningful sub-TLV change is observed. ze forms no encapsulation header, so what ze processes out of the TLV is the whole observable boundary

RFC9012-13-18.note: the attribute holding a meaningless VXLAN Encapsulation sub-TLV parses and both sub-TLVs enumerate; the negative (truncated TLV header refused) is a framing case, a neighbouring rule

RFC9012-13-19.note: round-trip of the TLV with the meaningless sub-TLV is byte-identical, so removal before distribution would fail the unit

RFC9012-13-3.note: TestRFC9012UnrecognizedTunnelTypeIsCarried: an attribute holding an unassigned tunnel type (0xFFFE) beside a type-15 TLV parses without error through ParseTunnelEncap and the recognized TLV's Preference is still read; the test fails if ParseTunnelEncap refused unknown types. Negative (TestRFC9012MalformedAttributeIsRejected, TLV length overrun refused) shows the parser is not blanket-accepting, a neighbouring framing rule (13-1/13-2) rather than a violation of this one

RFC9012-13-5.note: positive round-trips ParseTunnelEncap then TunnelEncap.WriteTo and asserts byte identity, so dropping the unrecognized TLV on re-encode fails it; the negative only shows the stripped encoding differs, which demonstrates the comparison can discriminate rather than exercising the producer

RFC9012-13-7.note: the RFC sentence covers the seven RFC 9012 single-instance sub-TLVs (Tunnel Egress Endpoint, Encapsulation, DS, UDP Destination Port, Embedded Label Handling, MPLS Label Stack, Prefix-SID); TestRFC9012DuplicateSingleInstanceSubTLVs duplicates the RFC 9830 Preference sub-TLV (type 12), which is not in that list, and ze decodes none of the seven (TunnelTLV.Preference in internal/core/bgp/attribute/tunnel_encap.go is the only sub-TLV reader). The assertions are correct evidence for RFC9830-2.4-1, which the same lines also tag, not for this row

RFC9012-13-8.note: positive duplicates the RFC 9830 Preference sub-TLV, not one of the RFC 9012 single-instance types the sentence names; ParseTunnelEncap and SubTLVs are type-blind so the behavior likely holds, but no buffer with a duplicated listed type (e.g. two Tunnel Egress Endpoint sub-TLVs) is asserted. The negative (stray trailing octet refused) violates the TLV framing rule, not this one

RFC9012-13-9.note: the sentence is the duplicate-sub-TLV paragraph's propagation clause; TestRFC9012AllSubTLVsPropagate round-trips one Preference and two unknown sub-TLVs with no duplicate, so an implementation that dropped second occurrences on propagation would pass this unit (duplicate round-trip is asserted only in the 13-8/13-7 unit, with a non-listed type)

RFC9012-3.1-3.note: a Tunnel Egress Endpoint sub-TLV with Reserved octets 0xA5 round-trips through ParseTunnelEncap/WriteTo byte-identically, so normalizing the Reserved subfield would fail it

RFC9012-3.2.1-2.note: a VXLAN Encapsulation sub-TLV with all R bits set round-trips byte-identically, so masking them on propagation would fail it

RFC9012-3.5-3.note: an Embedded Label Handling sub-TLV in a type-15 TLV (no VNI) is still enumerated and the attribute round-trips byte-identically, so stripping it before propagation would fail the unit

RFC9012-4.3-2.note: ParseExtendedCommunities then ExtendedCommunities.WriteTo reproduces a Color Extended Community's octets exactly for two distinct colors, so a changed value on propagation would fail it
